title: SQL FULL OUTER JOIN
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and row-preservation behaviour of SQL FULL OUTER JOIN.
Write valid SQLite queries using the join and an explicit ON condition.
Predict the effect of matching, unmatched and one-to-many rows.
Interpret NULL-extended columns and distinguish unmatched rows from matched values.
Recognize SQL dialect and database-version compatibility considerations.

understand.concept: FULL OUTER JOIN preserves all rows from both inputs. Matching pairs are combined; an unmatched left row has NULLs for right-side columns, and an unmatched right row has NULLs for left-side columns. Multiple matches produce multiple paired rows.
understand.whyItMatters: It is useful for reconciliation, comparing two datasets, and identifying records that exist on only one side of a relationship.
understand.analogy: It is like combining two complete lists, pairing entries with the same key and retaining unmatched entries from either list.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not show duplicate-key multiplication, three-valued logic, or differences in support among database engines.

examples.title: Create and inspect both inputs
examples.explanation: The sample includes customers without orders and an order without a customer.

examples.title: Preserve rows from both tables
examples.expectedOutput: Asha Rao | 101; Asha Rao | 102; Bilal Khan | NULL; Chitra Das | 103; Dev Patel | NULL; NULL | 104
examples.explanation: The result contains matched pairs plus unmatched customers and unmatched orders.

examples.title: Find only unmatched rows from either side
examples.expectedOutput: Bilal Khan | NULL; Dev Patel | NULL; NULL | 104
examples.explanation: The NULL test on each table's non-nullable primary key identifies which side lacks a partner.

examples.title: Reconcile row counts by match status
examples.explanation: The CASE expression classifies each result row into matched and unmatched groups.

examples.title: Compare full join with a left join
examples.explanation: A LEFT JOIN cannot preserve right-only rows; the full join can. SQLite added RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOIN support in version 3.39.0.

practise.guidedTask: Run the shared setup and execute each SQL FULL OUTER JOIN example. Before each query, mark which customer and order rows you expect to remain; then compare your prediction with the actual result.
practise.independentTask: Create departments and employees tables with at least five departments and six employees. Include at least one department with no employees and one employee with no department. Write five queries using the join type from this lesson, including one aggregate and one unmatched-row report.
hints: Start by identifying which table must be preserved.
Write the ON predicate using the actual relationship keys.
Add ORDER BY for deterministic output.
Use a non-nullable primary key to detect a missing match.
Check the DBMS version before relying on RIGHT or FULL OUTER JOIN.

options: Every row from the left input only
Every row from the right input only
questions.explanation: The selected join type determines which unmatched rows remain.

questions.prompt: Where is the relationship between the input rows normally specified?
questions.explanation: ON contains the join predicate that determines matching pairs.

questions.prompt: What can happen when one row matches two rows on the other side?
options: The row can appear twice in the result
The join changes to CROSS JOIN
questions.answer: The row can appear twice in the result
questions.explanation: A join returns matching row pairs, so one-to-many relationships multiply output rows.

questions.prompt: What is a safe way to avoid ambiguous column references?
options: Qualify columns with table names or aliases
Rename every column after the query
questions.answer: Qualify columns with table names or aliases
questions.explanation: Qualified names identify which input supplies a column.

questions.prompt: What should be checked when using this join across database engines?
questions.explanation: Join support and syntax details can vary by engine and version.
